newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thousands of German workers protest over sick pay.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of German workers protest over sick pay.

text.p: Thousands of engineering workers downed tools and demonstrated in the German state of Bavaria on Monday as another day of protest at cuts in sick pay got underway.
The IG Metall engineering union expects more than 150,000 people to take part in protests involving temporary stoppages in and outside their factories.
Several thousand workers gathered outside a truck assembly plant of MAN Nutzfahrzeuge AG in Munich on Monday morning.

The union has called on workers at more than 500 companies in Bavaria to join the protests to hammer home its opposition to a 20 percent cut in sick pay made possible by a law which came into force last month.

That law came into force in as part of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's austerity drive aimed at helping Germany fulfil strict fiscal requirements to qualify for a single European currency due for launch in 1999.
Workers outside the MAN factory carried placards which read, "We have reached the pain threshold," and "Hands off our sick pay -- 100 percent must stay."
Several thousand MAN workers and employees at aircraft engine maker MTU, a subsidiary of industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG, marched through their factories to the rally in Munich.
Monday's day of protest comes as the latest in a series which have included stoppages and disrupted production at German engineering companies, but which have stopped short of all-out strike action.
Protests have gone ahead despite earlier promises by employers not to introduce the sick pay cut until wider agreement with unions had been reached.
